Grouped K-NN or PCA Imputation

Source: R/group_imp.R
group_imp.Rd

Perform K-NN or PCA imputation independently within feature groups.

Usage

group_imp(
  obj,
  group,
  subset = NULL,
  allow_unmapped = FALSE,
  k = NULL,
  ncp = NULL,
  method = NULL,
  cores = 1,
  .progress = TRUE,
  min_group_size = NULL,
  colmax = NULL,
  post_imp = NULL,
  dist_pow = NULL,
  scale = NULL,
  coeff.ridge = NULL,
  threshold = NULL,
  row.w = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  nb.init = NULL,
  maxiter = NULL,
  miniter = NULL,
  solver = NULL,
  lobpcg_control = NULL,
  clamp = NULL,
  pin_blas = TRUE,
  on_infeasible = c("error", "skip", "mean")
)

Arguments

obj

A double matrix. Samples are in rows and features in columns.

group

A data frame or a character scalar. The feature groups, in one of these forms:

  • A character scalar naming a supported Illumina platform, such as "EPICv2". This needs the slideimp.extra package.

  • A long-format data frame with columns group and feature.

  • A list-column data frame with a feature list-column. Optional list-columns are aux, for auxiliary feature names, and parameters, for group-specific parameter lists.

subset

Optional character vector. The features to impute and return, by name, or NULL to impute every grouped feature and return every column. A group's other features become its auxiliary columns, and a group left with no feature is dropped with a message.

allow_unmapped

Logical. If FALSE, every column in colnames(obj) must appear in group. If TRUE, columns with no group assignment are left untouched and are not used as auxiliary columns.

k

Integer or NULL. Number of nearest neighbors for K-NN imputation. If NULL, k may be supplied through group$parameters.

ncp

Integer or NULL. Number of components for PCA imputation. If NULL, ncp may be supplied through group$parameters.

method

Character or NULL. One of "euclidean" or "manhattan" for K-NN imputation, or "regularized" or "EM" for PCA imputation. NULL uses "euclidean" for K-NN and "regularized" for PCA.

cores

Integer. Number of cores for K-NN imputation only, as described under Parallelization.

.progress

Logical. If TRUE, show progress.

min_group_size

Integer or NULL. Minimum total number of columns per group, counting both features and auxiliary columns. Groups smaller than this are padded with columns sampled at random from the other grouped columns of obj.

colmax

Numeric scalar between 0 and 1. Columns with a proportion of missing values greater than colmax take no part in the imputation, as described under Column mean fill.

post_imp

Logical. If TRUE, column means replace the missing values that remain after imputation, as described under Column mean fill.

dist_pow

Numeric. Power used to penalize more distant neighbors in the weighted average, where 0 gives an unweighted average. The weighting rule is given under Details in knn_imp().

scale

Logical. If TRUE, columns are scaled to unit variance.

coeff.ridge

Numeric. The ridge regularization for method = "regularized", ignored otherwise. Values below 1 move toward EM PCA, and values above 1 move toward mean imputation.

threshold

Numeric. Convergence threshold.

row.w

Numeric vector, "n_miss", or NULL. The row weights, normalized to sum to 1: positive values of length nrow(obj), "n_miss" to down-weight rows with more missing values, or NULL for equal weights.

seed

Integer, numeric, or NULL. Random seed used when padding small groups and, for PCA imputation, passed to pca_imp().

nb.init

Integer. Number of initializations. The first is always mean imputation, and the others are random.

maxiter

Integer. Maximum number of iterations.

miniter

Integer. Minimum number of iterations, at most maxiter.

solver

Character. One of "auto", "exact", or "lobpcg". The eigensolver. "auto" uses "exact" for small problems and otherwise runs a short timed probe, picking "lobpcg" only when it is clearly faster. With nb.init > 1, the choice from the first initialization is reused. See the PCA Performance tips section.

lobpcg_control

A list or NULL. LOBPCG control options, from lobpcg_control() or as a plain named list, or NULL for the defaults. Ignored when solver = "exact".

clamp

Numeric vector of length 2 or NULL. The bounds c(lower, upper) for PCA-imputed values, such as c(0, 1) for DNA methylation beta values, or NULL for none. Use -Inf or Inf for a one-sided bound. Observed values are not clamped.

pin_blas

Logical. If TRUE, pin BLAS threads to 1 on the mirai daemons in a parallel run. Defaults to TRUE.

on_infeasible

Character. One of "error", "skip", or "mean". The action for a group that is infeasible for imputation, for example because k or ncp is too large for the columns that colmax leaves. Defaults to "error".

Value

A slideimp_results object: a numeric matrix with the rows of obj and the columns that subset selects, with the missing values of the grouped features imputed.

Details

Imputing each group on its own can reduce the runtime for large matrices.

Specify k and related arguments to use K-NN imputation, or ncp and related arguments to use PCA imputation. If both k and ncp are NULL, group$parameters must supply either k or ncp for every group. Passing an argument of the other method, such as scale with k, is an error.

Group-specific parameters in group$parameters take priority over global arguments, and global arguments fill in the parameters a group does not set. All groups must use the same imputation method. A global argument shared with knn_imp() or pca_imp() that is NULL takes that function's default.

Per-group k is capped at the group's column count minus one, counting features and auxiliary columns. Per-group ncp is capped at the smaller of that cap and nrow(obj) - 2. group_imp() warns when it caps a value.

A group is infeasible when it is too small for any valid k or ncp, or when knn_imp() or pca_imp() cannot impute it, for example because colmax leaves too few columns. With on_infeasible = "skip", an infeasible group keeps its missing values. With "mean", column means fill them, and with "error", group_imp() stops with an error. A group whose features have no missing values is not imputed and is never infeasible. An infeasible group adds nothing to the mean_filled_cols and mean_filled_cells attributes of the result.

With subset, the result holds only the subset columns, in the order they have in obj. The other features still take part in the imputation, as auxiliary columns of their groups.

The mirai daemons run R's "L'Ecuyer-CMRG" generator. So with nb.init > 1, a parallel PCA run draws different random initializations from a sequential run under R's default generator. The two agree when the session also runs RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG").

Note

A platform name for group, such as "EPICv2" or "EPICv2_deduped", needs the optional slideimp.extra package. Its slideimp_arrays object lists the supported platforms.

Parallelization

  • K-NN: use the cores argument. If mirai daemons are active, cores is set to 1 to avoid nested parallelism.

  • PCA: use mirai::daemons() instead of cores.

  • With mirai daemons, each daemon runs BLAS on one thread unless pin_blas = FALSE.

Column mean fill

A column with a proportion of missing values greater than colmax takes no part in the imputation. The method neither uses the column to impute other columns nor imputes it.

With post_imp = TRUE, column means replace the missing values that remain after the method has run. Two kinds of missing value can remain: the missing values of the columns that took no part, and the cells for which the method found no value. Each column mean is the mean of the column's observed values. With post_imp = FALSE, both kinds stay missing.

The result records what the column means replaced, in two attributes:

  • mean_filled_cols: an integer vector with the index, in the result, of each column that took no part and was filled.

  • mean_filled_cells: an integer matrix with the columns row and col, one row for each cell that the method could not impute and that was filled.

Both attributes are empty when no column mean was used. print() reports them when they are not empty.

Missing values and non-finite input

obj must be a double matrix. An integer or logical matrix is rejected, not converted. Convert one with storage.mode(obj) <- "double".

NA and NaN are both treated as missing. The package does not distinguish between them.

Inf and -Inf are rejected on entry, and so is a column with no observed values (every cell NA or NaN). Locate them with which(is.infinite(obj), arr.ind = TRUE) and which(colSums(!is.na(obj)) == 0).

PCA Performance tips

Three arguments set the speed: solver, threshold, and scale. Tune these first, then the accuracy arguments ncp and coeff.ridge, on a representative subset.

Exact vs. LOBPCG. "lobpcg" suits large, approximately low-rank matrices with small ncp. "exact" suits small matrices, such as slide_imp() windows, where it is faster. It is also more reliable: it always converges, to eigenvectors exact to machine precision, while LOBPCG stops at the tolerance set in lobpcg_control() and can take many iterations, or reach maxiter, when the eigenvalues around the ncp-th one are close together. The warm start makes each later LOBPCG solve cheap: pca_imp() starts LOBPCG from the previous eigenblock and search direction, so once the imputed values stabilize, each solve takes a few iterations. The gain grows with the number of EM iterations, whatever the rank. solver = "auto", the default, chooses between the two and is a safe start.

Threshold. The default 1e-6 is conservative. 1e-5 is often faster and gives very similar values.

Scale. For columns on a common scale, such as DNA methylation beta values in [0, 1], scale = FALSE can be faster and more accurate.

BLAS. On Windows, the BLAS that ships with R can be slow, and OpenBLAS can replace it.

See Speeding up PCA imputation for the full workflow.

See also

  • prep_groups() to inspect and edit the groups and their parameters.

  • knn_imp() and pca_imp() to impute a single matrix.

Examples

set.seed(1234)
to_test <- sim_mat(10, 20, perc_total_na = 0.05, perc_col_na = 1)
obj <- to_test$input
group <- to_test$col_group
head(group)
#>    feature  group
#> 1 feature1 group2
#> 2 feature2 group1
#> 3 feature3 group1
#> 4 feature4 group2
#> 5 feature5 group1
#> 6 feature6 group1

# Simple grouped K-NN imputation
results <- group_imp(obj, group = group, k = 2, .progress = FALSE)
#> Imputing 2 groups using K-NN.
#> Running mode: sequential
results
#> Method: group_imp (K-NN imputation)
#> Dimensions: 10 x 20
#> 
#>          feature1  feature2  feature3  feature4   feature5  feature6
#> sample1 0.1568098 0.3213953 0.2768746 1.0000000 0.07839046 0.4219375
#> sample2 0.4098416 0.8658918 0.8221066 0.6396885 0.68926345 1.0000000
#> sample3 0.6801685 1.0000000 1.0000000 0.9953450 0.75246030 0.6958550
#> sample4 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.00000000 0.0000000
#> sample5 0.9639671 0.6409137 0.5111760 0.7184678 0.81815288 0.5883255
#> sample6 0.7031741 0.3731062 0.6782811 0.7542872 0.99910554 0.9070005
#> # Showing 6 of 10 rows and 6 of 20 columns

# Impute only a subset of features
subset_features <- sample(to_test$col_group$feature, size = 10)
knn_subset <- group_imp(
  obj,
  group = group,
  subset = subset_features,
  k = 2,
  .progress = FALSE
)
#> Imputing 2 groups using K-NN.
#> Running mode: sequential

# Use prep_groups() to inspect and edit per-group parameters
prepped <- prep_groups(colnames(obj), group)
prepped$parameters <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(prepped)), function(i) list(k = 2))
prepped$parameters[[2]]$k <- 4
knn_grouped <- group_imp(obj, group = prepped, .progress = FALSE)
#> Imputing 2 groups using K-NN.
#> Running mode: sequential

if (FALSE) { # interactive() && requireNamespace("mirai", quietly = TRUE)
# PCA imputation with mirai parallelism
mirai::daemons(2)
pca_grouped <- group_imp(obj, group = group, ncp = 2)
mirai::daemons(0)
pca_grouped
}
